messages:
sam_support: hey @maria — i just escalated a customer (AcmeCorp). their users can open the project UI but every action button (Edit, Invite, Billing) is greyed out. console API calls return 403. customer says this started after an idp config change last night. screenshot + logs: https://s3.redwood/support/acme/ss-01.png

maria_engineer: thanks. can you paste the exact API error and any id_token claims you have? sounds like a claim mapping got trimmed.

sam_support: copying the api response we get when calling GET /v1/projects/123 as the affected user:

```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "reason": "missing_role:project_admin",
  "hint": "required scope: project.admin"
}
```

and here's the base64-decoded id_token (redacted):

```
{
  "sub": "00u1abcd1234",
  "email": "alice@acme.com",
  "email_verified": true,
  "iss": "https://acme.okta.com",
  "groups": ["engineering"],
  // note: previously we expected an `app_roles` or `roles` claim here — it's absent
}
```

jordan_idp: fwiw we rolled an okta mapping that renamed `app_roles` -> `roles` last night. looks like token sessions issued before the change don't get the new claim until re-auth. scim provisioning still has the old mapping. could be a sync mismatch between SCIM and the live token claims.

clara_support: i just created a test user in their org and reproduced locally — UI buttons greyed and same 403. when i force re-login (invalidate session) the token includes `roles` again and access is restored. quick workaround: have affected users sign out/sign back in or we can trigger a session invalidation for the org.

sam_support: customer is enterprise, will be noisy to ask everyone to re-login. can we do a targeted fix?

maria_engineer: two short-term options:
1) run a SCIM resync to ensure SCIM group->role link is present in our backend for every user (doesn't fix existing sessions until they reauth, but console can consult SCIM on missing claims if we add the fallback).
2) grant a temporary org-level role to the affected users via console (manual) while we push a safer patch to login pipeline.

scim-bot: SCIM resync requested by @maria_engineer for org=acme id=org_9876
scim-bot: SCIM resync completed — 214 users updated (200 updated, 14 unchanged)

sam_support: i ran the resync with customer on the call — scim says updated but UI still grey for some users who haven't reauth'd yet. i pasted instructions to do a forced re-login to the customer. they want a non-interactive workaround (can't ask 200 users to reauth).

maria_engineer: long-term fix: add a login-layer fallback so if token misses `roles` we consult the latest SCIM snapshot for this user for role derivation. short-term plan: 1) run targeted session invalidation for org_9876 (affects active sessions only for that org) 2) support to grant a temp org-admin on a small list if needed. i'll prepare the invalidation job but need oncall approval.

oncall: be careful — invalidation will kick users out and could impact production workflows. limit to the single org and run at low-traffic window. approve pending runbook and communication.

clara_support: i'll assemble the minimal affected user list and offer the temporary manual grants while we schedule invalidation. customer agreed to a 10pm UTC window.

maria_engineer: i'll push a hotfix to add the SCIM fallback check in the auth pipeline today, but it won't be live for a few hours. after fallback goes live, resync + fallback should avoid requiring reauth for most cases.

sam_support: thanks all — i'll update the customer and schedule the invalidation with oncall at 22:00 UTC. i'll note the workaround for support cases in the ticket. :thumbsup:
